scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Monitoring ticket #9127: Hi, I'm covering the monitoring desk today and part
of the network has gone missing from the screens after one of the boxes was
restarted. The senior people keep saying the two parts were joined by
something called a "virtual link" and that traffic trying to cross it now
just disappears -- I couldn't tell you what a virtual link is, I'm afraid.
All I can see is that the far part is unreachable. Could someone please check
how the two parts are joined and reconnect them? Thank you!

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. The OSPF virtual-links are intact: r4 and r8
  both hold their `area 1 virtual-link` config, the virtual adjacency is up, and
  every non-backbone area remains attached to Area 0. PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
  (120.1.1.10) end to end with 0% loss, exercising a path that depends on the
  converged multi-area fabric. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case
  measures over-diagnosis of a virtual-link collapse that is not occurring (cf.
  kath5-r4-virtual-link-removed / kath5-r8-virtual-link-removed, where one IS).

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- a collapsed OSPF
virtual-link leaving an area unreachable -- is NOT reproducible: the r4<->r8
virtual adjacency is up (both endpoints still configure `area 1 virtual-link`,
each pointing at the other's router-id), and the transit chain stitching the
non-backbone areas to Area 0 is intact. End-to-end, PC0 (20.1.1.10) reaches PC12
(120.1.1.10) with 0% loss across the OSPF backbone + virtual-links + the EIGRP
domain, which it could not if a virtual-link on the path had collapsed.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the virtual-links are up and the
user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent checks the virtual-link state
(both endpoints present, adjacency up), confirms the affected area's prefixes are
still in the RIB, and exercises the PC0<->PC12 path -- all healthy -- and reports
no fault. An agent that "finds" a collapsed virtual-link or a stranded area --
blaming r4/r8 or re-adding a virtual-link that is already there -- is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I checked the OSPF virtual-link the team referred to and it is healthy. The virtual link is configured between r4 (ABR for areas 0 and 1) and r8 (ABR for areas 1 and 2). On r4, “show ip ospf neighbor” shows 18.1.4.1 Full on interface VLINK0, and r4’s OSPF reports “Number of full virtual adjacencies…: 1” in area 1. On r8, “show ip ospf neighbor” shows 14.1.4.1 Full on VLINK0 and its OSPF also reports one full virtual adjacency in area 1. Additionally, backbone routers (e.g., r3) have OSPF routes for r8’s area 2 prefixes (e.g., 80.0.0.0/8 via 34.1.1.2), proving LSAs are crossing the virtual link. End-to-end host reachability is intact (pc0 ↔ pc12 pings 0% loss).

Mechanism: If a virtual link were down, area 2 LSAs would disappear from area 0, and traffic to those networks would blackhole. That is not observed now.

Localization: OSPF virtual-link between r4 (Router-ID 14.1.4.1) and r8 (Router-ID 18.1.4.1) over area 1 is up on both endpoints.

Root cause: No active fault detected; the earlier “missing segment” likely occurred transiently while OSPF adjacencies (including the virtual link) reformed after a device reboot and monitoring caught the temporary gap.

Corrective fix: No change required now. To prevent recurrence, ensure OSPF router-ids are explicitly configured (to avoid ID changes after reboot that can break virtual-links) and confirm FRR services auto-start on all routers. Consider adding a monitor specifically for VLINK0 adjacency state on r4 and r8 to alert on future flaps.
